lead: First chapel on the right of the Puerta de los Hierros. Simple and silent, it houses one of the most valuable relics of the Christian world: the cup that, according to tradition, Jesus Christ used at the Last Supper.

The Chapel of the Holy Chalice in Valencia Cathedral was built as a Chapter House in 1365, served for holding the Cortes of the Kingdom and was the setting for Theology classes. It was not consecrated to the worship of the Holy Chalice until 1916. Today it is one of the most visited spaces in the city: a Gothic interior with a square plan, a star vault with the twelve Apostles and a 15th-century alabaster altarpiece that is one of the first works of the Renaissance in Spain.

From 30 October 2025 to 29 October 2026, Valencia Cathedral celebrates the Third Jubilee Year of the Holy Chalice, with the possibility of obtaining a plenary indulgence for pilgrims who meet the established conditions.

items.title: The Holy Chalice
items.subtitle: Oriental agate cup of the 1st century AD
items.body: The most important treasure of Valencia Cathedral and one of the most venerated objects in the Christian world. Tradition holds that it is the very cup Jesus Christ used at the Last Supper. The cup is made of oriental agate — of the carnelian variety, dark red — dated to the 1st century BC. It measures approximately ten centimetres in diameter and seven in height. The base is a small boat-shaped piece of very translucent chalcedony edged in gold, added in the Middle Ages. Alfonso the Magnanimous donated it to the Cathedral in 1437; in 1916 it was moved to this chapel. Until 1744 it was used regularly in the liturgy.
facts: Oriental agate (carnelian) cup · Medieval base of chalcedony and gold
1st century BC · Medieval base and handles added later
Alfonso V the Magnanimous donated it to the Cathedral in 1437
Since 1916 · Protected in a glass case above the altarpiece

items.title: The Chapel · Former Chapter House
items.subtitle: Flamboyant Gothic · 1365–1369 · 13×13 m · 16 m high
items.body: The chapel was built between 1365 and 1369 on the commission of Bishop Vidal de Blanes to serve as a Chapter House and burial place for bishops and canons. The Cortes of the Kingdom of Valencia were held here and Theology classes were taught. It was not consecrated to the worship of the Holy Chalice until 1916. It is a space with a square plan, with smooth walls of dark carved stone and three windows with polychrome stained glass. Built initially detached from the Cathedral, it was joined to the main building by a passageway in the last decade of the 15th century, by the master stonemasons Pere Compte and Asensi Fos.
facts: 1365–1369 · Commissioned by Bishop Vidal de Blanes
Square plan of 13×13 m · 16 m high
Chapter House · Cortes of the Kingdom · Theology classes
To the worship of the Holy Chalice in 1916

items.title: The Star Vault
items.subtitle: Eight ribs · The twelve Apostles on the bosses
items.body: The Gothic vault of the Chapel of the Holy Chalice is one of the most beautiful and complex examples of Valencian Gothic. Eight ribs and twenty-four tierceron arches form an eight-pointed star that rests on polychrome corbels. On the bosses of the vault, also polychrome, appear the twelve Apostles; on the central boss appears the coronation of the Virgin in heaven after the Assumption. Looking up in this space is one of the most striking moments of any visit to Valencia Cathedral.
facts: The twelve Apostles on the bosses · Polychrome
Coronation of the Virgin after the Assumption
Polychrome corbels at the springing of the ribs

items.title: The Alabaster Altarpiece
items.subtitle: Antoni Dalmau and Julià lo Florentí · 1441–1446
items.body: The great Gothic alabaster altarpiece that frames the Holy Chalice was carved between 1441 and 1446 by the architects Antoni Dalmau and Julià lo Florentí, with the participation of the sculptors Joan de Sagrera, Joan de Sogorb and Arnau de Bruselas. It was originally the central door of the Cathedral’s choir screen, through which canons and bishops entered in procession. In 1777 it was moved to this chapel when the choir screen was replaced by a neoclassical one. The twelve reliefs in the upper part, the work of Julià lo Florentí, are among the first manifestations of the Renaissance in Spain: the lower scenes represent the Old Testament and the upper ones the New, in a parallel typological reading.
facts: Antoni Dalmau, Julià lo Florentí, Joan de Sagrera, Arnau de Bruselas
Alabaster · Gothic style with details of the early Renaissance
12 scenes · OT (lower) and NT (upper) in typological reading
One of the first works of the Renaissance on the Iberian Peninsula

items.title: The Marseille Chains and the Canvases
items.subtitle: Alfonso V the Magnanimous · 1423 · Vicente López · Nicolás Florentino
items.body: On the left of the chapel hang enormous chains of 226 links that closed the port of Marseille, brought to Valencia by Alfonso V the Magnanimous in 1423 as a war trophy. Above them is the canvas “Expulsion of the Moriscos”, by Vicente López, court painter to Ferdinand VII. On the other side, the fresco of the Adoration of the Kings, painted by Nicolás Florentino, completes the pictorial programme of this singular space where the political, military and religious history of Valencia merge in one corner.
